decision.summaryForCoordinator: I reviewed the v3 extraction immediately before this one and rejected it on a finding that rests on facts about THIS file, so I had a direct interest in v1 being sound and ran the review looking for reasons to reject it. It survives. The two central checks pass by construction rather than by reading: the harness object is EQUAL to the live parent's DR-G01 entry by object equality, and the promised artifactPathWhenAuthored string resolves character-for-character to this subject's own path — which is the property that distinguishes it from the v2 and v3 extractions and makes its occupancy claim true of itself. The parent pin equals the live parent digest and is the only 64-hex string in the file. The D-006 trap is avoided the same way it was in v3, and inherited from the same accepted parent: bare integers are 1, 25 and 26214400; MiB, 1024 and 1048576 all return zero; both 26214400 mentions are negations present verbatim in the parent's own entry; and the unit is held open as UNDECIDED with size comparison deferred to a D-006 unit successor while exclusion membership is scored now. I pressed two things hard and both resolved in the artifact's favour. First, 'For each of the four platforms' looked like it contradicted D-002's two operating systems — but the accepted parent uses four-platform language consistently across DR-G01, DR-G02 and DR-G05, and four is the right unit for download and packaging gates, where the signed artifact ships per OS-architecture pair. It does not conflict with the permission family's two, which applies where architecture is STATED INVARIANT. Second, the mtimes are counterintuitive: the file numbered v1 was written at 03:13:09, after v2 at 03:02:05. But v1 makes no lineage or precedence claim, and the version number is forced by the parent's own path string, so nothing false is asserted. One thing I must correct in my own record. In the v3 verdict I wrote that the defective authorityClaim sentence 'is also present in v1'. That was loose. v1's sentence stops at 'is occupied' where v3's continues 'against the accepted parent', and v1's is TRUE because v1 is the promised path. The v3 finding is unaffected — it rested on v3's own text and location, both re-confirmed here — but that incidental remark about v1 is withdrawn. Two smaller notes: the 'independently reviewed parent' claim is true and chronologically sound, the parent verdict having landed at 03:11:23 before this file at 03:13:09, but it is unpinned, and the later v3 extraction already carries the parentReview digest that would fix that; and v1 lacks the explicit does-not-SATISFY, does-not-close-OBL-2 and does-not-authorize-implementation negations that v3 added, which cost nothing here because those tokens do not occur at all, but are worth carrying back if this file is ever revised. Codex is usage-limited per the dispatch; I named the Codex path, no Codex file exists, and I neither read nor authored one, so this is a single independent review. Fourteen attacks run, fourteen refuted, zero findings.
